findings.evidence: Round 1 finding IC-008 was partially resolved: the intent now explicitly includes "next stage" in the `/stage` command description. However, the push-blocking git hook—offered in KIT-DESIGN as an optional backstop ("optionally a hook blocking `git push` while the gate hasn't passed")—is not mentioned in INT-0001 either as in-scope or deferred.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether the push hook is in scope for 0001 or listed under Out of scope. If not implemented here, add one line: e.g., "Push-blocking hook deferred; CI verifier is the backstop."

findings.evidence: The Functional section states the change spans two repos and produces "two PRs: dogs-app code PR and lab-admin code PR, both part of the code stage, listed per repo in plan.md." Success criterion 6 specifies "a code PR changing a file not listed in plan.md fails plan drift." It is unclear whether (a) `/stage code <NNNN>` opens one PR per repo (two separate verifier runs) or one unified PR; (b) plan.md has per-repo sections or a single plan covers both; (c) plan drift is evaluated per-repo or across both together.
findings.recommendation: Owner to clarify the multi-repo code-stage flow: Is `/stage code <NNNN>` invoked once or twice? Does plan.md have per-repo sections or is lab-admin plan separate? Is plan drift checked independently per repo, or must the owner coordinate changes across both?

findings.evidence: The model section states: "reviewers run on smaller models (Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 4.5, set per agent); Opus 5.5 only for the main session and for authoring **plans and code**." This covers stages 3 and 4. Stages 1 (intent) and 2 (spec) authoring are not mentioned; it is ambiguous whether the author uses Opus 5.5 for all stages.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the author's model for all stages: e.g., "Author uses Opus 5.5 for intent and spec authoring as well" (by analogy with plans and code), or specify which model is used for stages 1–2.
